champion: Cystoid macular edema secondary to anastrozole therapy
ordered_diagnoses: Cystoid macular edema secondary to anastrozole therapy

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral visual disturbance with associated ocular inflammation and cystoid macular edema
salient_findings: Blurry vision in the right eye for several months
Cystoid macular edema with subfoveal fluid in the right eye
Epiretinal membrane in the left eye
key_facts: Patient is a 65-year-old woman
Blurry vision in the right eye for several months
History of bilateral iritis
Amblyopia in the left eye
Bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens
Left-sided mastectomy 2.5 years prior
On anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years
Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/150 OS
Intraocular pressures were normal
Right eye showed trace conjunctival injection and 2+ fine keratic precipitates
Dilated fundus examination revealed cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye
Epiretinal membrane in the left eye
No inflammation in the periphery was noted in either eye
OCT showed significant cystoid macular edema and subfoveal fluid in the right eye
Fluorescein Angiography revealed cystoid macular edema with leakage in both eyes
Blood tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders were within reference limits

s4.champion: Cystoid macular edema secondary to anastrozole therapy

raw.champion: Cystoid macular edema secondary to anastrozole therapy
raw.rationale: The patient's history of anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years, along with the presence of cystoid macular edema in both eyes as shown by OCT and fluorescein angiography, supports this diagnosis. Anastrozole has been associated with cystoid macular edema as a side effect.

rejected.label: Birdshot chorioretinopathy
rejected.why: Typically presents with distinctive birdshot lesions in the retina, which were not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Intermediate uveitis
rejected.why: Characterized by inflammation in the vitreous and peripheral retina, which was not noted in this patient.

rejected.label: Uveitic macular edema
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of iritis, the current presentation and diagnostic tests do not strongly support active uveitis as the primary cause of the macular edema.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Blood tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders, including those that might suggest sarcoidosis, were within reference limits, making this diagnosis less likely without further supporting evidence.
